capex.heading: Future Capital Expenditures
capex.text:
Management currently estimates that the Company’s funding requirements for the next twelve months will exceed $2.0 million. The Company is currently pursuing an uplisting of its common stock from the OTC market to the Nasdaq Capital Market. If the uplisting is successfully completed and market conditions are favorable, the Company may seek to raise additional capital through one or more equity financings. There can be no assurance that the Company will successfully complete the uplisting or that any financing will be available on acceptable terms, or at all.

Any proceeds from future financings, if completed, are expected to be used primarily to fund the Company’s working capital requirements, application development, content licensing, marketing and user acquisition activities related to the development and promotion of its mini-drama application, expenses associated with the proposed uplisting, and other general corporate purposes.

The Company may require additional financing to fund its operations and planned business activities. If the Company is unable to obtain sufficient additional financing when needed, it may be required to reduce, delay or discontinue certain planned operations and expenditures, including marketing and application development activities, dispose of assets, seek protection under applicable bankruptcy laws, or pursue other strategic alternatives.

intro.text: Hartford Creative Group, Inc. (“HFUS,” “we,” “us,” or “Company”) was originally incorporated in the State of Nevada on April 2, 2008 under the name PhotoAmigo, Inc. It changed its name to Hartford Great Health Corp. on August 22, 2018. On May 11, 2024, the Company further changed its name to Hartford Creative Group, Inc. The Company is a media and marketing company. Following its exit from its legacy hospitality and early childhood education operations, the Company has, since January 2024, concentrated on two principal lines of business: (i) social media advertising and related marketing services in China, and (ii) a mini-drama content business, which includes a short-form drama streaming application launched in the United States.

s.t: Advertising placement services accounted for approximately 97.4% of total net revenues, compared with approximately 98.2% in the prior year, and increased by approximately 33.7% year over year.
For the years ended July 31, 2026 and 2025, the remaining 2.6% of net revenues, or $71,600, and 1.8% of net revenues, or $36,000, respectively, were generated from the Company’s mini-drama business.

The payment of dividends is within the discretion of the Board and will depend on our earnings; capital requirements; financial condition; prospects; applicable Nevada law; and other factors our Board might deem relevant.

However, revenues generated under the framework agreements will depend on the execution of individual service orders, customer advertising spending levels, market conditions, and other factors, and there can be no assurance regarding the amount or timing of revenues that may ultimately be realized from such arrangements.

These framework agreements establish potential advertising service arrangements with the customers; however, the amount and timing of revenue that may ultimately be recognized will depend on the actual services provided, customer orders or other applicable contractual conditions, and the Company’s satisfaction of the applicable revenue recognition requirements.
The timing and amount of any resulting revenue will depend on market acceptance, user engagement, customer demand, monetization of the platform, and other factors.

While management expects the Company’s mini-drama application business to generate U.S. taxable income in future years, the deferred tax asset specifically related to GILTI depends upon the repatriation of previously taxed earnings from its PRC subsidiaries.
The realization of deferred tax assets depends on the generation of sufficient taxable income in the relevant jurisdictions and periods.

During the year ended July 31, 2024, we recorded net income of $1,092,874, noncash adjustments for a deferred tax asset of $204,901 a $1,315,786 increase of contract liabilities, a $1,327,509 increase of accounts payable, a $336,077 increase of other current payable, a $22,100 increase of related party payables, and offset by a $2,423,493 increase of advance to contract, a $573,790 increase of accounts receivable and $26,275 increase of prepaid and other current receivable.

wc.text: As of July 31, 2025, we had a working capital deficit of $105,739 comprised of current assets of $6,508,395 and current liabilities of $6,614,134. This represents a decrease of $3,460,226 in the working capital deficit from the July 31, 2024 amount of $3,565,965. The improvement was primarily due to the forgiveness of $2.5 million in related party payables and the positive operating results for fiscal year end of 2025. We had an accumulated deficit of $4,811,733 compared to $5,910,843 at the previous year end. To date, we have funded our operations through short-term debt and equity financing.

capex.heading: Future Capital Expenditures
capex.text:
We believe that our funding requirements for the next twelve months will be in excess of $2,000,000. We are currently seeking further funding through related parties’ loan and finance.

We are in the process of uplisting the Company’s stock from the OTC market to the Nasdaq exchange. Assuming all conditions are met in our favor, we plan to raise capital through either debt or equity financing. The proceeds from this financing will be used to cover the costs related to the uplisting procedure.

ocf.l: Net Cash Provided by (Used in) Operating Activities

cor.text: Operating Cost and Expenses: Cost of revenue decreased significantly to $7,081 for the year ended July 31, 2026, compared with $112,618 for the year ended July 31, 2025, a decrease of $105,537, or approximately 93.7%. Because the Company recognizes revenue from its advertising placement services on a net basis, the related costs are net to gross revenue amount and generally not included in cost of revenue. Cost of revenue for the year ended July 31, 2026 primarily consisted of costs associated with the Company’s mini-drama content. In comparison, cost of revenue for the year ended July 31, 2025 primarily consisted of outsourced consulting service costs. The Company did not incur comparable outsourced consulting service costs during the year ended July 31, 2026, resulting in the significant decrease in cost of revenue.

oi.text: Income tax expense: The income tax recognized for the fiscal years ended July 31, 2026 and 2025 resulted primarily from income taxes on the operating income of the Company’s China-based operations and the deferred tax effects of temporary differences. Income tax expense was $804,524 for the year ended July 31, 2026, compared to $172,011 for the year ended July 31, 2025. The increase in income tax expense for fiscal 2026 was primarily due to higher current income taxes on the Company’s China-based operations and a valuation allowance of $350,845 recorded against the deferred tax asset related to GILTI; see Note 8—Income Taxes to our Consolidated Financial Statements. The net deferred tax assets are expected to reduce future income tax liabilities.

ga.text: During the year ended July 31, 2026, selling, general and administrative expenses increased to $777,943 from $697,416 during the year ended July 31, 2025. The increase was primarily driven by increased directors’ and officers’ (D&O) insurance premiums and higher audit fees. In addition, the Company recorded a credit loss expense of $497,966 for the year ended July 31, 2026, reflecting an allowance for expected credit losses established against accounts receivable that remained uncollected as of July 31, 2026, with no comparable charge in the prior year. This provision was the principal driver of the increase in total operating cost and expenses for fiscal 2026.

sga.text: During the year ended July 31, 2026, selling, general and administrative expenses increased to $777,943 from $697,416 during the year ended July 31, 2025. The increase was primarily driven by increased directors’ and officers’ (D&O) insurance premiums and higher audit fees. In addition, the Company recorded a credit loss expense of $497,966 for the year ended July 31, 2026, reflecting an allowance for expected credit losses established against accounts receivable that remained uncollected as of July 31, 2026, with no comparable charge in the prior year. This provision was the principal driver of the increase in total operating cost and expenses for fiscal 2026.

prov.text: During the year ended July 31, 2026, the Company generated net income of $641,767 and recorded a non-cash credit loss expense of $497,966, a non-cash deferred tax adjustment of $191,956 and a gain on forgiveness of lease liability of $5,609. These amounts were offset by a net decrease of approximately $1,963,000 from changes in operating assets and liabilities. The principal usage of operating cash related to a decrease in contract liabilities of $4,764,048 and an increase in accounts receivable of $911,604, offset by a decrease in advance to contractors of $2,848,913, an increase in other current payable of $768,690, and an increase in accounts payable of $101,032.

nonop.text: Other (expense) income: Other expense, net amounted to $14,748 for the year ended July 31, 2026, compared to other income, net of $45,944 for the corresponding period of 2025. The change primarily reflected the absence in fiscal 2026 of a $21,362 gain on the disposal of subsidiaries and an approximately $21,000 local government grant recognized in fiscal 2025. In addition, the Company incurred net interest expense of $15,389 in fiscal 2026, compared with net interest income of $3,137 in fiscal 2025.

tax.text: Income tax expense: The income tax recognized for the fiscal years ended July 31, 2026 and 2025 resulted primarily from income taxes on the operating income of the Company’s China-based operations and the deferred tax effects of temporary differences. Income tax expense was $804,524 for the year ended July 31, 2026, compared to $172,011 for the year ended July 31, 2025. The increase in income tax expense for fiscal 2026 was primarily due to higher current income taxes on the Company’s China-based operations and a valuation allowance of $350,845 recorded against the deferred tax asset related to GILTI; see Note 8—Income Taxes to our Consolidated Financial Statements. The net deferred tax assets are expected to reduce future income tax liabilities.

net.text: Net Income: We recorded net income of $641,767, or $0.03 per share, for the year ended July 31, 2026, compared to net income of $1,099,110, or $0.04 per share, for the year ended July 31, 2025, due to the factors discussed above.

ocf.heading: Operating Activities
ocf.text:
Cash used in operating activities was $636,298 for the year ended July 31, 2026, as compared to $13,094 for the year ended July 31, 2025.

During the year ended July 31, 2026, the Company generated net income of $641,767 and recorded a non-cash credit loss expense of $497,966, a non-cash deferred tax adjustment of $191,956 and a gain on forgiveness of lease liability of $5,609. These amounts were offset by a net decrease of approximately $1,963,000 from changes in operating assets and liabilities. The principal usage of operating cash related to a decrease in contract liabilities of $4,764,048 and an increase in accounts receivable of $911,604, offset by a decrease in advance to contractors of $2,848,913, an increase in other current payable of $768,690, and an increase in accounts payable of $101,032.

During the year ended July 31, 2025, we recorded net income of $1,099,110, noncash adjustments for a deferred tax asset of $195,588 and a disposal gain of $21,362, an increase in contract liabilities of $3,514,536, a decrease in accounts receivable of $529,532, and an increase in other current payable of $154,320. These were offset by an increase in advance to contractors of $3,834,924 and a decrease in accounts payable of $1,285,101.

wc.text: As of July 31, 2026, we had working capital of $749,187 comprised of current assets of $4,568,285 and current liabilities of $3,819,098. This represents an improvement of $854,926 from the July 31, 2025 working capital deficit of $105,739. The improvement was primarily due to the positive operating results for the fiscal year ended July 31, 2026. We had an accumulated deficit of $4,169,966 compared to $4,811,733 at the previous year end. To date, we have funded our operations through short-term debt and equity financing.

capex.heading: Future Capital Expenditures
capex.text:
Management currently estimates that the Company’s funding requirements for the next twelve months will exceed $2.0 million. The Company is currently pursuing an uplisting of its common stock from the OTC market to the Nasdaq Capital Market. If the uplisting is successfully completed and market conditions are favorable, the Company may seek to raise additional capital through one or more equity financings. There can be no assurance that the Company will successfully complete the uplisting or that any financing will be available on acceptable terms, or at all.

Any proceeds from future financings, if completed, are expected to be used primarily to fund the Company’s working capital requirements, application development, content licensing, marketing and user acquisition activities related to the development and promotion of its mini-drama application, expenses associated with the proposed uplisting, and other general corporate purposes.

The Company may require additional financing to fund its operations and planned business activities. If the Company is unable to obtain sufficient additional financing when needed, it may be required to reduce, delay or discontinue certain planned operations and expenditures, including marketing and application development activities, dispose of assets, seek protection under applicable bankruptcy laws, or pursue other strategic alternatives.

lines.name: Cash and cash equivalents
lines.why: Cash can repay debt or be paid out: a financial asset. Cash needed to run the business is operating; move it if you know how much.

lines.name: Receivables
lines.why: Owed by customers for sales: operating.

lines.name: Inventory
lines.why: Goods held for sale: operating.

lines.name: Prepaid and other current assets
lines.why: Prepayments and other operating items: operating.

lines.name: Property, plant and equipment
lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease right-of-use assets
lines.why: Leased stores, offices and equipment used in the business: operating.

lines.name: Deferred tax assets
lines.why: Taxes on operating income paid ahead: operating.

lines.name: Other non-current assets
lines.why: Other long-term operating items: operating.

lines.name: Accounts payable
lines.why: Owed to suppliers for operations: operating.

lines.name: Accrued liabilities
lines.why: Services and other costs not yet paid: operating.

lines.name: Deferred revenue
lines.why: Customers' payments ahead of delivery: operating.

lines.name: Income taxes payable
lines.why: Taxes on operating income: operating.

lines.name: Other current liabilities
lines.why: Other operating items due within a year: operating.

lines.name: Short-term debt and commercial paper
lines.why: Borrowed money: financial.

lines.name: Finance lease liabilities
lines.why: Leases that work like a loan for the asset: financial.

lines.name: Operating lease liabilities
lines.why: Rent owed on leases used in the business: operating by default. Move it to financing to treat leases like debt (if the balance sheet has no lease line of its own, they sit inside other liabilities).

lines.name: Other current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current assets minus the current lines above: current assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current assets (total assets − current assets) minus the non-current lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current liabilities minus the current lines above: current liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current liabilities (total liabilities − current liabilities) minus the non-current lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

accounts.name: Equity
accounts.note: Other comprehensive income (currency translation, unrealised gains) moves equity without passing through net income: it is in the residual.
